hypothesis: One-token lazy parsing will improve size by skipping a match when the next-position match is at least two bytes longer.
change_summary: Add optional cl mode with one-byte lookahead; preserve greedy mode and v1 decoder format.
notes: -0.937% size overall; Canterbury -2.261%; encode speed -18.992%; no per-file size regressions; no external Pareto point. Full results: results/exp-0001/.

hypothesis: Independent 64 KiB blocks with raw fallback will eliminate incompressible expansion and reduce match-state memory without unacceptable aggregate regressions.
change_summary: Add v2 cb/clb modes with nine-byte raw-or-LZ block headers and strict version-aware decoding.
notes: Versus v1 lazy: size -4.503%; encode +24.273%; decode +3.549%; encoder RSS -44.828%. Canterbury size +7.106%; raw/scientific/RGB about -11%. Retain v1 for cross-block compression. Full results: results/exp-0002/.

hypothesis: Block-static entropy coding of LZ token payloads will close a meaningful part of the Canterbury and structured-text gap after exact table costs.
change_summary: Add cbh/clbh modes that select the smallest of raw, plain LZ, or serialized-tree Huffman-coded LZ per v2 block.
notes: Versus blocked lazy: size -9.606%; encode -12.902%; decode -20.754%; RSS +4.425%. Canterbury -22.057%; no per-file size regressions; 1.509% larger than gzip-1 and slower. Full results: results/exp-0003/.

hypothesis: Two-byte matches for distance <=1024 and length <=35 will outweigh four-byte escapes and improve the blocked size/speed frontier.
change_summary: Test an exact-selected variable-match payload beside fixed LZ; revert implementation after rejection.
notes: Versus blocked lazy: size -1.161%; encode -37.960%; decode -7.119%; RSS +5.900%. Nearly all size gain came from generated pseudo-executable; only four small Canterbury files improved. Full results: results/exp-0004/.

hypothesis: Seeding each 64 KiB block with up to 65,535 prior bytes will recover cross-boundary matches while preserving raw fallback and bounded state.
change_summary: Add cblink/clblink v2 mode 4 with one prior-window match history and no second parse.
notes: Versus independent lazy: size -2.286%; encode -20.386%; decode +0.556% noise; RSS +4.734%. Recovers nearly all v1 structured-category ratio with bounded state. Screen and validation: results/exp-0005-screen/ and results/exp-0005/.

hypothesis: Exact-selected Huffman coding over linked-history token payloads will compound the two strongest size mechanisms and approach gzip-1 size.
change_summary: Add cblinkh/clblinkh v2 mode 5 selecting raw, linked LZ, or serialized-tree Huffman-linked LZ.
notes: Versus independent Huffman lazy: size -2.002%; encode -22.589%; decode -5.227%; RSS +18.927%. Size is 0.523% below gzip-1, but zstd-1 remains smaller and faster. Screen and validation: results/exp-0006-screen/ and results/exp-0006/.

hypothesis: Separating controls, literals, offset bytes, and lengths into field-specific order-0 alphabets will outperform one mixed token-byte Huffman alphabet after all tree costs.
change_summary: Add cblinks/clblinks v2 mode 6 with five exact-counted Huffman streams over the unchanged linked token sequence.
notes: Versus linked joint Huffman: size -7.773%; encode -19.257%; decode -7.651%; RSS +5.435%; no per-file size regressions. 0.383% smaller than zstd-1 but zstd-3 is smaller and faster. Results: results/exp-0007-screen/ and results/exp-0007/.

hypothesis: Limiting lazy lookahead to current matches under 32 bytes will recover encode speed with negligible aggregate ratio loss.
change_summary: Add clblinksg mode using the retained mode-6 format with a fixed 32-byte lazy-search gate.
notes: Versus full max lazy: size +0.087%; encode +8.188%; RSS -2.344%. Decode timing was inconsistent across screen/validation. Generated source +9.318%; generated text -12.066%; Canterbury +0.074%. Results: results/exp-0008-screen/ and results/exp-0008/.

hypothesis: A data-driven reversible byte-delta at an adaptively selected stride 1-8 will expose compressible structure in raw RGB and scientific blocks.
change_summary: Add clblinksd mode 7: histogram-concentration stride prefilter, reversible delta, independent LZ, and split entropy with exact total-size selection.
notes: Versus mode 6: size -34.804%; encode -20.374%; decode +2.733% noise; RSS -12.401%. RGB -99.655%, scientific -10.593%; no Canterbury change. Creates a dev-corpus encode frontier but is synthetic-data-heavy. Results: results/exp-0009-screen/ and results/exp-0009/.

hypothesis: An 8-bit Huffman prefix table for sufficiently large streams will improve decode throughput without changing the compressed representation.
change_summary: Build a 256-entry lookup for Huffman streams with >=256 symbols; retain tree fallback and dslow control.
notes: Versus identical-stream tree decoder over five repeats: decode +10.837%; size/encode/binary/RSS unchanged. Scientific +50.69%, JSON +23.44%, XML +22.47%, Canterbury +9.42%; some low-benefit categories regress slightly. Results: results/exp-0010-screen/ and results/exp-0010/.

hypothesis: Four previous-byte-class literal alphabets will exploit local structure that one order-0 literal model misses.
change_summary: Test an exact-selected mode with four literal Huffman streams keyed by the previous decoded byte's top two bits; revert after rejection.
notes: Versus delta parent over five repeats: size -0.258%; encode throughput -11.319%; decode throughput -4.535%; encoder RSS +19.940%. Mode 8 won 29/152 blocks across seven files, but 83.6% of the 6,084-byte gain came from generated pseudo_text.bin. Results: results/exp-0011-screen/ and results/exp-0011/.

hypothesis: Persistent circular match chains will remove repeated linked-history indexing while preserving token choices and compressed size.
change_summary: Test clblinksp with a 64-bit head table and circular predecessor-distance array; verify byte-identical output and revert after rejection.
notes: Compressed streams were byte-identical to clblinksd. Over five repeats encode throughput fell 7.132%; decoder throughput differed -2.772% despite identical streams and is noise. The 64-bit hot head table and ring indirection outweighed saved history indexing; generated source alone improved 2.15%. Results: results/exp-0012-screen/ and results/exp-0012/.

hypothesis: A small spatial sample plus a conservative concentration gate will retain useful delta strides while avoiding full histogram scans and discarded transformed parses.
change_summary: Add clblinksdf using at most 4,095 sampled bytes from block start/middle/end and require a 1.2x concentration gain before transformed parsing.
notes: Compressed streams were byte-identical to clblinksd on all 26 dev files. Over five repeats encode throughput improved 15.261% with unchanged size/format; decode -1.316% is identical-stream noise and the RSS maximum was not credited. Selector work fell from 52 transformed parses to 36 while retaining all 34 winning blocks. Results: results/exp-0013-screen/ and results/exp-0013/.

hypothesis: A lazy decision based on estimated raw token-bit density will outperform the current covered-length rule across data distributions.
change_summary: Test a 25-bit match versus 33-bit literal-plus-match local density rule with an upper-bound lookahead gate; revert codec after dual-corpus rejection.
notes: Frozen dev screen: 44 bytes smaller (-0.0019%), encode -0.420%, with 8 files better and 8 worse. Public research screen: 1,407 bytes larger (+0.0326%), encode -6.723%, 4/16 files better and 12/16 worse. Rejected without validation; raw token density did not generalize. Results: results/exp-0014-screen/ and results/exp-0014-research-screen/.

hypothesis: Modulo deltas between consecutive match distances will make the split distance streams more compressible.
change_summary: Test an exact-selected mode 8 that delta-codes the 16-bit distance sequence before the existing low/high Huffman streams; revert after dual-corpus null result.
notes: Mode 8 won zero blocks across 26 dev and 16 public research files, leaving every compressed size unchanged. Generating the extra five-stream representation reduced encode throughput 8.870% on dev and 6.547% on research. Results: results/exp-0015-screen/ and results/exp-0015-research-screen/.

hypothesis: A work-estimated Huffman lookup gate will avoid table construction on streams whose tree-walk savings cannot repay it.
change_summary: Test dwork on identical clblinksdf streams; enable the 256-entry lookup only when encoded-bit work exceeds one edge per symbol plus 2,048 construction edges.
notes: Five-repeat identical-stream decode improved 1.736% on dev and 0.712% on public research, below the established ~3% process-level noise threshold; 5/26 dev and 3/16 research files still regressed. Reverted rather than tune the threshold. Results: results/exp-0016-screen/, exp-0016/, exp-0016-research-screen/, and exp-0016-research/.

hypothesis: The unchanged work-estimated Huffman lookup gate will show a reproducible steady-state decode gain once process startup is removed.
change_summary: Re-test EXP-0016 unchanged with the in-process runner; retain dwork after two reversed-order 30-repeat runs on both routine suites.
notes: Identical size/format. Dev decode +3.038% then +3.746%; public research +1.217% then +0.622%, with sign preserved after reversing codec order. Prior process controls showed unchanged encode/binary/RSS. 60 sanitizer-backed d/dwork streams passed. Results: results/exp-0017-inprocess-dev*/ and results/exp-0017-inprocess-research*/.

hypothesis: A bounded dynamic parser using the parent block's actual split-Huffman field costs will improve ratio broadly enough to justify a maximum-compression mode.
change_summary: Add clblinksopt: precompute longest matches at every position, derive literal/distance/length code costs from the parent parse, optimize literals versus the eight longest match lengths, and exact-select the resulting ordinary mode-6 stream.
notes: Versus clblinksdf over three repeats: dev size -2.509%, encode -70.307%, decode -3.422%, encoder RSS +10.843%; 17/26 files improve and none regress. Public research size -3.616%, all 16 files improve, encode -74.007%, decode -2.968%, RSS +31.471%. Production binary grows 23.816% versus pre-feature. Results: results/exp-0018-screen/, exp-0018/, exp-0018-research-screen/, and exp-0018-research/.

hypothesis: Skipping bounded dynamic parsing when the parent split-Huffman representation does not beat raw storage will recover encode speed without changing selected output.
change_summary: Test clblinksoptg with a parent-split-versus-raw work gate; verify exact streams on all observed files, then revert after the speed gain fails to generalize.
notes: Five-repeat dev output is byte-identical and encode throughput improves 4.239%, but three generated fixtures (random, pseudo_text, RGB) account for 64.6 ms saved versus 59.1 ms aggregate; the remaining dev files regress in aggregate. Public research output is also byte-identical but encode throughput regresses 0.578%. Screen research timing falsely suggested +6.6%; validation reversed it. Results: results/exp-0019-screen/, exp-0019/, exp-0019-research-screen/, and exp-0019-research/.

hypothesis: Re-estimating split-Huffman costs from EXP-0018's optimized parse and parsing once more will capture model/parse convergence gains across data distributions.
change_summary: Add clblinksopt2: run exactly one additional cost-model and whole-block DP pass, Huffman-code it as ordinary mode 6, and exact-select it against the first optimized parse.
notes: Versus clblinksopt over three repeats: dev size -0.482% with 15/26 files improved and none worse, encode throughput -39.758%, encoder RSS +7.200%; public research size -0.498% with 14/16 improved and none worse, encode -42.289%, RSS +11.258%. Decode format is unchanged and timing deltas are not credited. Candidate remains dominated by cached xz-6 on dev, so this is an internal maximum-ratio point, not an external frontier claim. Results: results/exp-0020-screen/, exp-0020/, exp-0020-research-screen/, and exp-0020-research/.

hypothesis: For each candidate match length, selecting the lowest modeled-cost distance from the bounded hash chain will beat using only the longest match's distance.
change_summary: Add clblinksopt2d: after EXP-0020's two passes, run one exact-selected DP whose eight candidate lengths each use the lowest split-Huffman distance cost among up to 64 chain matches.
notes: Versus clblinksopt2 over three process repeats: dev size -0.737% with 15/26 files improved and none worse, encode throughput -68.119%, encoder RSS +62.439%; public research size -0.767% with all 16 files improved, encode -47.595%, RSS +11.330%. A three-repeat in-process dev control measures decode -0.377% (280.09 versus 281.15 MB/s), rejecting the noisy process-level -10.4% result. Binary size and decoder representation are unchanged. Cached xz-6 still dominates this internal endpoint. Results: results/exp-0021-screen/, exp-0021/, exp-0021-research-screen/, exp-0021-research/, and exp-0021-inprocess-dev/.

hypothesis: Enumerating costed-distance matches inside the backward DP and storing only the selected offset will preserve EXP-0021's stream while reducing encoder memory without slowing it.
change_summary: Add clblinksopt2df: build predecessor chains once, enumerate the same bounded candidates during backward optimization, and replace eight offsets per position with one selected offset.
notes: Streams are byte-identical to clblinksopt2d on all 43 observed files. Over three repeats, dev encoder RSS falls 11.931% and public research RSS falls 10.253%; encode throughput changes -0.091% and +0.297%, both noise. Decode, compressed size, format, and binary behavior are unchanged; the compiled binary grows only 32 bytes versus EXP-0021. Results: results/exp-0022-screen/, exp-0022/, exp-0022-research-screen/, and exp-0022-research/.

hypothesis: Sharing one immutable predecessor-chain and longest-match index across all optimized parses will preserve EXP-0022's stream while recovering substantial encode speed.
change_summary: Add clblinksopt2dfs: build the per-block match index once, reuse longest matches for both normal DP passes, and reuse predecessor chains for fused costed-distance enumeration.
notes: Streams are byte-identical to clblinksopt2df on all 43 observed files. Over three repeats, dev encode throughput improves 15.709% with RSS +0.746%; public research improves 25.347% with RSS +3.777%. Size, format, and decode behavior are exact controls; process decode differences are noise. The compiled binary is 92,552 bytes (+96 versus EXP-0022). Results: results/exp-0023-screen/, exp-0023/, exp-0023-research-screen/, and exp-0023-research/.

hypothesis: Exact-selecting joint-Huffman and split-Huffman models for each optimized parse will recover blocks where five split trees cost more than field separation saves.
change_summary: Test joint mode-5 encoding of all three already-generated optimized token streams against their mode-6 encodings, then revert after a dual-corpus zero-win result.
notes: Candidate streams are byte-identical to clblinksopt2dfs on all 43 observed files, proving optimized joint Huffman wins zero blocks. One-repeat encode screens change -1.776% dev and -1.688% public research; timing was not validated because deterministic size supplied no positive signal. Parent mode 5 already covers joint-coding wins from the original parse. Results: results/exp-0024-screen/ and exp-0024-research-screen/.

hypothesis: When the first optimized parse is byte-identical to its parent, skipping the provably redundant second normal DP will preserve output and recover meaningful encode speed.
change_summary: Test an exact token-stream fixed-point check; on equality, reuse the first parse as the cost model for the costed-distance pass and skip the second normal parse plus split encode.
notes: Streams are byte-identical to clblinksopt2dfs on all 43 observed files, confirming correctness of the fixed-point rule. One-repeat encode screens improve only 0.439% on dev and 0.011% on public research, both far below the 3% process-noise threshold; no validation was warranted. The exact condition is too rare or covers too little work to create a practical point. Results: results/exp-0025-screen/ and exp-0025-research-screen/.

hypothesis: Conditioning match-distance alphabets on short (4-7 byte) versus longer matches will capture length/distance dependence and improve optimized compression broadly enough to justify its model cost.
change_summary: Add an exact-selected seven-stream block mode with two distance-low/high Huffman contexts; build conditional costs from the iterated parse and reuse EXP-0023's shared match index for a fused costed-distance DP.
notes: Full 21-mode testing passed all 36 inputs. Dev size improves 9,226 bytes (-0.406%) but only pseudo_text.bin, generated JSON, and kennedy.xls change; public Calgary+Large improves just 26 bytes (-0.000634%) on one geo block. The candidate selects mode 8 in 33 observed blocks but encode throughput falls 42.529% dev and 37.026% research. The local dependency is real but does not generalize broadly enough to retain, so implementation and mode were reverted. Results: results/exp-0026-screen/ and exp-0026-research-screen/.

hypothesis: Reusing exact split-Huffman code costs already built during encoding will eliminate redundant demultiplexing and tree construction across optimized parse stages and produce a meaningful encode-speed gain with identical output.
change_summary: Add an isolated stats-sharing mode that returns literal/distance/length code costs from each existing split encode and feeds them directly to the next DP while retaining EXP-0023's shared match index.
notes: All 42 dev+research compressed streams are byte-identical to clblinksopt2dfs and full 21-mode testing passed 36 inputs. One-repeat process screens improve encode throughput only 0.789% dev and 1.184% research, below the 3% validation threshold; RSS changes -0.739%/-0.475% and decode changes are noise. No repeated validation was warranted. Redundant Huffman-stat recovery is measurable but not a major maximum-mode bottleneck, so the implementation was reverted. Results: results/exp-0027-screen/ and exp-0027-research-screen/.

hypothesis: Scoring each chain candidate's modeled distance once into one of eight eligible-length buckets, then suffix-propagating the best cost and nearest-offset tie break, will preserve every EXP-0023 choice while materially accelerating the final DP.
change_summary: Add clblinksopt2dfsb: retain the shared match index, replace the final distance selector's up-to-eight rescans per candidate with one cost evaluation plus an exact eight-bucket suffix minimum, and leave prior modes unchanged.
notes: All 42 dev+research compressed streams are byte-identical to clblinksopt2dfs and full 21-mode testing passed 36 inputs. Exact-commit three-repeat validation improves encode throughput 15.635% on dev and 8.247% on Calgary+Large; 19/26 dev and all 16 research files are faster. Size, format, decoder work, dev RSS, and 92,552-byte binary size are exact controls; process decode variation is noise because streams and decoder are identical. Results: results/exp-0028-screen/, exp-0028/, exp-0028-research-screen/, and exp-0028-research/.

hypothesis: A single literal alphabet of residuals from the previously decoded byte will capture useful local context without EXP-0011's extra Huffman trees.
change_summary: Prototype an exact-selected mode-8 split representation with byte-difference literals, then remove it after the dual-corpus screen.
notes: One-repeat startup-free screening saves only 28 bytes on dev and zero bytes on Calgary+Large. Raw text byte-difference entropy is substantially worse than order-0 byte entropy, and constructing the unused representation adds work. The mode was removed. RSS was not measured. Results: results/exp-0029-literal-residual-screen/ and exp-0029-literal-residual-research-screen/.

hypothesis: Canonical Huffman codes with packed or sparse length metadata will preserve split-stream bit costs while broadly reducing five-tree model overhead.
change_summary: Add clblinksopt2dfsbc and block mode 8; exact-select old-tree or compact-canonical coding per split field and the complete representation per block.
notes: Versus clblinksopt2dfsb, dev size improves 17,588 bytes (-0.775%) across 16/26 files with none worse; public research improves 102,572 bytes (-2.501%) and all 16 files. Three-repeat startup-free decode changes +0.13%/-0.65%; process dev encode changes -3.04% and RSS +11.75%. All normal/boundary tests and 42-file ASan+UBSan round trips pass. The 111,832-byte binary is +20.83% versus EXP-0028. Results: results/exp-0030-compact-models*/.

hypothesis: A 16 MiB history and 24-bit distances will find cross-block matches missed by the 64 KiB format.
change_summary: Add seven-stream wide mode 9 with a 16 MiB window and cost-aware offset selection.
notes: Dev improves 30,280 bytes and public research reaches 3,702,339 bytes. It beats xz-6 on the frozen dev aggregate but still trails xz on research. Results: results/exp-0031-wide-history-costed32-*.

hypothesis: Coarse previous-byte classes will improve literal entropy without a large model.
change_summary: Prototype two/four/eight-class literal contexts and duplicate the wide parse for exact selection.
notes: Four classes win the sample gate, but full gains are only 811 dev bytes and 1,043 research bytes while parse work nearly doubles. Results: results/exp-0032-wide-context*.

hypothesis: Adaptive arithmetic coding will beat compact Huffman on skewed split fields.
change_summary: Add mode 10 and exact per-field selection between adaptive arithmetic and compact Huffman.
notes: Improves dev by 26,226 bytes and research to 3,643,645 bytes; all research files improve. Results: results/exp-0033-wide-arithmetic-*.

hypothesis: Order-1 byte arithmetic contexts will improve wide split streams.
change_summary: Add mode 11 with previous-symbol adaptive arithmetic models.
notes: Only 865 sample bytes improve and decode slows materially; retained only as an exact fallback because several structured dev streams later select it. Results: results/exp-0034-wide-arithmetic-order1-sample-screen/.

hypothesis: Previous-output literal classes will improve adaptive literal coding.
change_summary: Add streaming context arithmetic literals as mode 12.
notes: Only 923 sample bytes improve over EXP-0033 and speed falls; retained only as a structured-file fallback. Results: results/exp-0035-wide-arithmetic-context-sample-screen/.

hypothesis: A bounded static arithmetic model will reduce adaptive cold-start overhead.
change_summary: Add dense/sparse static frequency headers and exact selection as mode 13.
notes: Improves dev by 33,301 bytes and research by 27,266 bytes versus EXP-0033. Results: results/exp-0036-wide-arithmetic-static-*.

hypothesis: Parsing with static arithmetic Shannon costs will align match choices with the retained coder.
change_summary: Add one Q8 static-cost DP pass and exact-select its ordinary mode-9-to-13 encoding.
notes: Improves dev by 12,945 bytes and research by 17,868 bytes. Results: results/exp-0037-static-cost-parse-*.

hypothesis: A second static-cost iteration will converge model and parse further.
change_summary: Repeat static-cost estimation and DP once more.
notes: Improves dev by 2,532 bytes and research by 6,639 bytes with about 13% more encode time. Results: results/exp-0038-static-cost-parse2-*.

hypothesis: Larger fixed blocks will reduce framing and expose longer matches.
change_summary: Raise the maximum-ratio block size from 64 KiB to 1 MiB.
notes: Improves dev by 60,490 bytes and research by 53,896 bytes; three dev files regress under the fixed rule. Results: results/exp-0039-large-block-*.

hypothesis: A 16 MiB whole-file block will use the full wide window and remove remaining framing.
change_summary: Raise the size-max block cap to 16 MiB.
notes: Improves research by 4,685 bytes and dev by 118 bytes with negligible measured time change. Results: results/exp-0040-whole-block-*.

hypothesis: Deeper hash chains will uncover distant matches on large files.
change_summary: Raise longest-match search to 512 and cost search to 64.
notes: Improves research by 25,456 bytes but drops encode throughput sharply. Results: results/exp-0041-deep-match-*.

hypothesis: Considering 32 nearby match lengths will improve the DP.
change_summary: Double the eligible length suffix from 16 to 32 candidates.
notes: Saves only 93 sample bytes and grows code; implementation removed. Results: results/exp-0042-length32-sample-screen/.

hypothesis: An extreme 1024/128 match search will find additional size-max opportunities.
change_summary: Raise longest-match and cost chains to 1024 and 128.
notes: Improves dev by 4,974 bytes and research by 16,588 bytes; encode throughput is only 0.108 MB/s on research. Results: results/exp-0043-extreme-match-*.

hypothesis: Running the full extreme parse on transformed data will close structured-file gaps.
change_summary: Prototype a second full extreme parse after delta transformation.
notes: The targeted gate exceeded five minutes on four files and was terminated before a valid benchmark. Replaced by the bounded EXP-0045 design.

hypothesis: A cheap sampled delta transform plus shallow wide parse will capture structured numeric data.
change_summary: Add outer mode 14 with sampled stride and block-local 256/32 transformed parsing.
notes: Improves dev by 48,585 bytes and research by 1,785 bytes with no full-corpus regressions. Results: results/exp-0045-wide-transform-cheap-*.

hypothesis: Conditioning distance bytes on match length will capture residual dependence.
change_summary: Add mode 15 with four length contexts for distance bytes.
notes: Wins zero bytes on text and binary gates while adding work. Results: results/exp-0046-distance-context-*.

hypothesis: A full previous-byte literal bit tree will exploit literal dependencies without serialized tables.
change_summary: Add mode 16 with a streaming 256-context adaptive binary tree and evaluate it once on the final parse.
notes: Improves dev by 7,085 bytes and research by 23,191 bytes versus EXP-0045. Results: results/exp-0047-literal-bit-context-final-dev-screen/ and optimized-research-screen/.

hypothesis: Using the last match byte as an expected-bit predictor will improve literals immediately after matches.
change_summary: Add mode 17 with LZMA-style matched-literal subtrees until the first mismatching bit.
notes: Improves research by 13,862 bytes and all 16 files; sample improves 4,122 bytes. Results: results/exp-0048-matched-literal-*.

hypothesis: Persisting the last-distance predictor across literal runs will extend matched-literal gains.
change_summary: Apply the predictor to every later literal until another match.
notes: Regresses the fixed sample by 1,628 bytes and is slower; immediate-post-match semantics restored. Results: results/exp-0049-persistent-matched-literal-sample-screen/.

hypothesis: A gradually trusted coarse order-2 context will improve matched literal probabilities without cold-start damage.
change_summary: Mix the order-1 model with previous-byte plus high-nibble-of-previous2 contexts and exact-select mode 18.
notes: Improves research by 4,736 bytes across nine files and sample by 3,057 bytes. Results: results/exp-0050-mixed-matched-literal-*.

hypothesis: Full order-2 context on ordinary literal bits will outperform the coarse table.
change_summary: Use a 65,536-context fallback-mixed tree only after matched prediction is inactive.
notes: Improves the sample by 1,110 bytes overall but regresses one file by 16 bytes when replacing EXP-0050; retained only inside later exact-selected mode 20. Results: results/exp-0051-full-order2-literal-sample-screen/.

hypothesis: Modulo deltas between consecutive 24-bit distances will create zero-heavy streams.
change_summary: Transform distance bytes before ordinary exact-selected entropy coding.
notes: Wins zero bytes on all sample files and adds about 2% encode time; encoder and mode removed. Results: results/exp-0052-delta-distances-sample-screen/.

hypothesis: Binary match/literal decisions conditioned on eight-token history will beat packed control bytes.
change_summary: Add mode 20 with fallback-mixed control arithmetic and full order-2 literals.
notes: Observed research improves 3,152 bytes over EXP-0050 and 13 files; restoring EXP-0050 coexistence removes two tiny prototype regressions. Results: results/exp-0053-control-context-*.

hypothesis: Four-token control history will generalize better than eight-token history.
change_summary: Reduce the control context mask from eight prior bits to four.
notes: Five bytes worse overall with mixed per-file results; eight-token history restored. Results: results/exp-0054-control-history4-sample-screen/.

hypothesis: A hashed order-3 literal context will capture common trigrams.
change_summary: Add an exact-selected 65,536-context order-3 candidate.
notes: Wins zero sample bytes and adds table work; mode removed. Results: results/exp-0055-order3-literal-sample-screen/.

hypothesis: Scoring 256 distance candidates instead of 128 will find cheaper known offsets.
change_summary: Double only the cost-aware distance chain.
notes: Saves 744 sample bytes but increases encode time 37.5%; 128 restored. Results: results/exp-0056-cost-chain256-sample-screen/.

hypothesis: A 2048 longest-match chain will uncover still-hidden distant matches.
change_summary: Double longest-match discovery depth while keeping cost scoring at 128.
notes: Improves corrected EXP-0053 research size by about 9,977 bytes and helps ten files; encode throughput falls sharply. Results: results/exp-0057-match-chain2048-*.

hypothesis: A four-entry move-to-front recent-distance cache will omit raw distances for repeated offsets.
change_summary: Add exact-selected mode 22 with eight streams: rep code plus raw distances only for cache misses.
notes: Final same-run dev aggregate beats xz-6 by 251,670 bytes (14.65%). Public research is 3,423,757 bytes versus xz-6 3,363,140: Bite trails 60,617 bytes (1.80%), encodes about 40.8x slower there, and uses 282,771,456-byte peak encode RSS. All 26 dev files, 16 MiB boundaries, malformed headers, and representative ASan+UBSan paths pass. Results: results/exp-0058-rep-distances-*/ and exp-0058-final-*-external/.

hypothesis: Substituting an equivalent recent distance in a forward pass will increase rep hits without changing match lengths.
change_summary: Exact-select a rep-preferred offset stream against EXP-0058.
notes: Improves all three samples but only by 124 bytes; not promoted to full corpus and removed from final encode path. Results: results/exp-0059-rep-preferred-sample-screen/.

hypothesis: Extending valid recent-distance matches beyond parser-selected lengths will make rep-aware parsing materially better.
change_summary: Add a forward exact-selected recent-match extension candidate with explicit byte validation.
notes: Produces exactly EXP-0059's sample bytes while increasing encode time 45.7%; candidate removed. Explicit-choice byte validation retained as a safety improvement. Results: results/exp-0060-rep-extended-sample-screen/.

hypothesis: Pricing recent-distance cache states during parsing will improve the final representation.
change_summary: Add a forward rep-aware reparse with a four-entry recent-distance cache and exact selection against EXP-0058.
notes: Improves the fixed sample by 391 bytes (0.031%) but is too small to justify promotion. Results: results/exp-0061-rep-aware-sample-screen/.

hypothesis: Offering more bridge lengths to the rep-aware parser will uncover useful cache transitions.
change_summary: Expand recent-distance match choices beyond the 16 longest lengths.
notes: One byte worse than EXP-0061 and slower; the narrower choice set was restored. Results: results/exp-0062-rep-aware-bridge-sample-screen/.

hypothesis: A second rep-aware model/parse iteration will converge to a smaller stream.
change_summary: Rebuild the model from EXP-0061 and run the rep-aware pass once more.
notes: Only four bytes smaller than EXP-0061 while adding substantial work. Results: results/exp-0063-rep-aware-iterated-sample-screen/.

hypothesis: A bounded beam carrying exact recent-distance state will outperform the greedy rep-aware pass.
change_summary: Add a width-four stateful beam over literals, raw matches, and four cached distances.
notes: Improves EXP-0058 by 460 bytes and EXP-0061 by 69 bytes on the fixed sample, still only 0.036% overall. Results: results/exp-0064-rep-beam4-sample-screen/.

hypothesis: Doubling beam width will preserve more valuable recent-distance states.
change_summary: Increase the rep-state beam from four to eight entries.
notes: Saves only three bytes beyond width four; width four restored. Results: results/exp-0065-rep-beam8-sample-screen/.

hypothesis: Training raw-distance costs only on cache misses will correct the rep-aware objective.
change_summary: Build distance-byte models from code-4 misses instead of every original match distance.
notes: Only three bytes smaller than EXP-0061 and one byte larger than EXP-0063. Encode timing is invalid because the machine was suspended during the run. Results: results/exp-0066-rep-miss-costs-sample-screen/.

hypothesis: xz-6 is not a sufficient state-of-the-art target for Bite.
change_summary: Run Bite and available high-ratio presets of xz, zstd, and Brotli together on the independent 16-file research corpus.
notes: Brotli 11 is strongest at 3,283,714 bytes. Bite EXP-0058 is 3,423,757; xz-9e 3,360,808; zstd-19 3,384,473. Results: results/exp-0067-strong-references-research/.

hypothesis: A general high-order model for very small byte alphabets will close Bite's dominant E. coli deficit.
change_summary: Add exact-selected mode 23: alphabet serialization plus adaptive order-4 arithmetic coding for blocks with at most eight symbols.
notes: Improves E. coli by 75,465 bytes to 1,127,219, beating Brotli 11 there by 10,639 bytes. Independent aggregate is 12,516 bytes smaller than xz-9e and 64,578 bytes (1.97%) larger than Brotli 11. All 16 research and 26 development files round-trip; development size is unchanged; ASan+UBSan mode-23 and truncation checks pass. Results: results/exp-0068-small-alphabet-order4-{research,dev}/.

hypothesis: Evaluating every LZ candidate before selecting mode 23 wastes nearly all E. coli encode time.
change_summary: Add a separate fast preset with small-alphabet early return, 1024-deep discovery, 64-deep distance costing, and only the final wide representation.
notes: E. coli is byte-identical at 1,127,219 bytes and 673x faster in the full run. Research is 2.85x faster than EXP-0068 and remains 5,369 bytes smaller than xz-9e. Results: results/exp-0069-fast-pareto-research-screen/.

hypothesis: A 48-entry distance-cost chain will retain most modeled-distance benefit at lower parse cost.
change_summary: Reduce only the fast preset distance-cost chain from 64 to 48.
notes: Costs 680 bytes and saves 14.13 seconds versus EXP-0069 while remaining 4,689 bytes smaller than xz-9e. Results: results/exp-0070-fast-cost48-research-screen/.

hypothesis: A 32-entry distance-cost chain will remain below xz-9e while improving speed further.
change_summary: Reduce only the fast preset distance-cost chain from 48 to 32.
notes: Costs 1,122 bytes and saves 7.55 seconds versus EXP-0070; remains 3,567 bytes smaller than xz-9e. Results: results/exp-0071-fast-cost32-research-screen/.

hypothesis: A 16-entry distance-cost chain may be the fastest setting that preserves the public xz-9e size win.
change_summary: Reduce only the fast preset distance-cost chain from 32 to 16.
notes: Research is 1,536 bytes smaller than xz-9e and 4.76x faster than EXP-0068; development is 1,482,255 bytes and 4.13x faster than EXP-0068. All 42 corpus files round-trip; ASan+UBSan and truncated mode-23 rejection pass. Results: results/exp-0072-fast-cost16-{research,dev}-screen/.

hypothesis: An 8-entry distance-cost chain will locate the speed preset's xz-size boundary.
change_summary: Reduce only the fast preset distance-cost chain from 16 to 8.
notes: Saves 2.38 seconds but is 904 bytes larger than xz-9e, so depth 16 is restored. Results: results/exp-0073-fast-cost8-research-screen/.

hypothesis: A general variable-order literal model can reduce the remaining text gap without file-specific gates.
change_summary: Exact-select mode 24: retained order-1/order-2 literal models plus cautiously trusted tagged hashed order-3 and four-character word-suffix contexts.
notes: Research improves 1,173 bytes over EXP-0068, beating xz-9e by 13,689 bytes while trailing Brotli 11 by 63,405. Development improves 261 bytes to 1,466,005. All 42 files round-trip; ASan+UBSan mode-24 and truncation checks pass. Peak RSS is unavailable because the environment blocked the process memory sampler. Results: results/exp-0074-context-mix3-tuned-{research,dev}-inprocess/.

hypothesis: Block sorting captures long text contexts that the current LZ parser leaves expensive.
change_summary: Exact-select mode 25 (cyclic BWT, move-to-front, zero runs, adaptive order-1 arithmetic) in cmax; add cmax, cbwt and cfast presets.
notes: On main. cmax on research; timing from results/m1-2-timing-research (one M1, process harness, 3 repeats). 36,487 bytes below Brotli 11. cbwt alone: 3,373,378 bytes in 3.23 s. bsc and zpaq (EXP-0080) are smaller. Acceptance checks in RESEARCH_PLAN.md still pending.

hypothesis: Exact-selecting the mode-25 BWT alongside the cfast candidates matches cmax size at a fraction of its encode time.
change_summary: Fast preset combining cfast candidates with BWT; no new decoder format.
notes: Running in its own local session. Estimate from existing per-file results: min(cfast, cbwt) = 3,247,583 research bytes.

hypothesis: Context-mixed binary coding of the BWT output beats the move-to-front, zero-run, order-1 second stage.
change_summary: Add mode 26 (context-mixed BWT second stage) and the cbwt2 preset; existing modes unchanged.
notes: Research -12.44% vs cbwt, 10.05% below Brotli 11 and 0.9% below bsc max; zpaq -m5 still smaller. Timings are cloud in-process (not comparable): about 4x cbwt to encode, 10x to decode. m1-2 process timing queued.

hypothesis: An LZ mode with static tANS tables decodes within 1.5x of zstd -19 while staying smaller.
change_summary: Work in progress: block mode 27 and the cdec preset.
notes: Cloud session still running.

hypothesis: Logistic mixing of more literal contexts closes the gap to Brotli 11 on the small Calgary files.
change_summary: Add mode 28 (context-mixing literal model) and the ccm preset, exact-selected with every cmax candidate.
notes: Research corpus not yet measured (cloud host was blocked). Generated dev files: 721,843 vs cmax 906,048 (-20.3%); tuning samples -22.2% (not independent). m1-2 research run queued.

hypothesis: Practical codecs understate the size targets; block-sorting, PPM and context-mixing references set a stronger bar.
change_summary: Add bzip2, bsc, PPMd (7-Zip), zpaq and optional cmix references to the harness and measure them.
notes: Merged into main. Research sizes: zpaq -m5 2,806,383; bsc max 2,980,242; bsc 3,002,482; PPMd 3,045,785; bzip2 -9 3,364,810. Cloud timings only; m1-2 timing queued. cmix still pending.

hypothesis: A pre-registered modern hold-out corpus guards against overfitting as parallel experiments multiply.
change_summary: Lock holdout-2026 (37 files, 144,681,868 bytes) with pinned hashes and an evaluation protocol.
notes: Merged into main. No compressor has been run on the hold-out files.

hypothesis: Running independent candidate work on worker threads cuts cmax wall time at least 2x without changing output.
change_summary: BITE_THREADS worker pool for the wide match search, candidate encodes and per-block candidates; default 1 thread.
notes: Output identical to cmax by design. Byte-identical in 36 local checks; m1-2 identity check on all 41 files running. Loaded laptop: book1 cmax 10.9 s to 5.8 s at 8 threads.

hypothesis: SA-IS on the doubled block sorts BWT rotations several times faster with byte-identical output.
change_summary: Sort aperiodic blocks with SA-IS and keep prefix doubling for periodic ones; tests check both sorters agree.
notes: Merged into main: output is byte-identical, so it cannot regress. Identical in 20,041 differential checks and on all 41 dev and research files on m1-2. Laptop CPU sort time 1.4-2.2x faster. Also fixes the macOS --sanitize abort.
